results.likelyCause: When onExit vetoes a context.go, go_router 14.8.1 GoRouterDelegate.setNewRoutePath (~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/go_router-14.8.1/lib/src/delegate.dart:249-261) keeps the old configuration. The current (detail) location then appears to be reported to the browser again as a new history entry. The app wires onExit in frontend/lib/core/router.dart:36-37,70,94,110.

observations.detail: 'Save changes' and 'Unsaved changes' sit below the fold of the upper pane (y≈655, behind the tab bar at y≈512), so the user must scroll the upper pane to reach them. A click at the button's semantic position lands on the dispute list below instead. This isn't caused by the theme change: an earlier semantics dump showed the same position. The button itself is painted at 153x38 and saves once scrolled into view (server phone 555-7906).

With unread notifications, the '99+' badge (19x16 at 1165,23; on phone 303,23) covers the bell's centre and swallows taps. On a clean page a click on the badge does nothing (URL unchanged); a click on the lower-left of the bell opens #/notifications. Likely cause: the Positioned badge Container is stacked over the IconButton in frontend/lib/shared/widgets/app_shell.dart:181-190 and wins the hit test.

observations.area: Sales POC picker (D-18, not part of this fix set)
observations.detail: On the invoice form, typing the full username 'vu-sales-mu2ylll4f82e' in 'Choose Sales POC' left the list unfiltered (AURRC…, AURSB…). Adding and deleting a space made it filter to the one user. So D-18 is still present in PocPicker; the new SearchPickerField does not have this lag.

After B was cancelled, the promise card still showed 'INV-20260915-0432 • ₹100.00 left' for the cancelled invoice, while the edit dialog says 'no longer owed'. The chip uses the balance with no status check: frontend/lib/features/promises/promises_tab.dart:186.
At 400x820 the invoice number still breaks mid-token ('INV-20 / 26091 / 5-0428').

POST /api/disputes as admin returns 403 'You do not have permission for this action', so the test disputes were opened with the customer's login. Only one open dispute per invoice is allowed (400 'An open dispute already exists for this invoice'). Admin detail screens do show a 'Raise dispute' button; its behaviour for admin was not exercised here.
